plugin.name: Browser Use
plugin.description: Let the agent drive a real browser: navigate, read pages, fill forms, click and sign in.
view.console.label: Browser Use
view.console.description: Browser runtime status and how to use it
hero.tagline: Let the agent actually open a browser, click through pages and fill forms — instead of handing back a summary of the web.
console.title: Browser Use
console.installHint: First use requires installing the browser automation runtime (~90MB). If no Chrome is installed, Chrome for Testing is downloaded as well.
console.outdatedHint: Found agent-browser {{found}}, but this plugin needs {{required}} or newer. Upgrade installs the pinned version into Vetta's own runtime directory and leaves your existing global install untouched.
console.chromeFound: System Chrome detected; it will be reused, no extra download needed.
console.chromeMissing: No system Chrome detected. One more download (Chrome for Testing) is needed before you can start.
console.readyHint: The agent-browser CLI is ready. Ask the agent to open a page; every Agent conversation uses an independent browser session.
guide.capabilities.label: What it can do
guide.cap.navigate.title: Open a page and actually read it
guide.cap.navigate.body: Navigate anywhere and locate elements through an accessibility-tree snapshot — cheaper on context than screenshots, more precise than raw HTML.
guide.cap.interact.title: Really operate the page
guide.cap.interact.body: Click, fill, check, select, scroll, wait for elements — roughly anything a person can do in a page.
guide.cap.signin.title: Sign in once, stay signed in
guide.cap.signin.body: The window is right in front of you, so captchas and 2FA are yours to handle. The agent can use a stable restore key or profile when sign-in state must persist.
guide.cap.isolation.title: Isolated accounts
guide.cap.isolation.body: Every Agent task uses an independent session. Multiple media accounts in one task use separate account-keyed sessions and sign-in state.
guide.vs.label: How this differs from web search
guide.vs.body: Web search returns someone else's summary. It cannot open pages behind a login and cannot change anything. Browser Use opens a real browser: it can get into an admin panel, fill a form, page through to result 3 and export what it finds. Use search to look something up; use this to get something done.
guide.prompts.label: Try saying
guide.prompts.hint: Click to copy, then adapt it to your case.
guide.prompt.read: Open https://news.ycombinator.com and use a snapshot to put the top 10 titles and links into a table.
guide.prompt.signin: Open https://example.com/admin. I'll sign in myself in the window that pops up — after that, pull this month's orders into a table.
guide.prompt.form: Open this signup form and fill it in with the details below, but don't submit — let me review first: name Jane Doe, email jane@example.com.
guide.prompt.compare: Open these two product pages and compare price, stock and estimated delivery in one table.
guide.cli.label: CLI execution
guide.cli.direct: The agent calls agent-browser directly through the shell without loading an additional browser-specific Tool.
guide.cli.independent: Every Agent conversation has a unique session ID and does not share its active page with other conversations or the Plugin API.
guide.cli.accounts: Multiple accounts use different session suffixes and restore keys so their cookies and local storage remain separate.
guide.cli.upstream: For complex operations the agent reads the core skill bundled with the installed version, avoiding command-reference drift.
guide.cli.hint: Commands in one task reuse its private CLI session. Closing it does not delete persistent restore/profile data.
guide.newSession: Browser commands in this conversation use an independent CLI session; a new conversation will not take over its active page.
footer.credit: Browser automation is provided by vercel-labs/agent-browser (Apache-2.0). This plugin installs the runtime and contributes its CLI Skill to the agent.
